title: Gradual commitment credits lab
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight 'gradual commitment' product that sits between pure PAYG and full reserved capacity. Target: SMBs + startups that want lower unit cost without a heavy contract.

Top-level idea (one-liner): sell time-boxed small commitments (1–3 months) in exchange for progressively deeper discounts as commitment duration and upfront-signal increase. Allow credits to be consumed both as session credits and token credits, with conversion rules.

Key design goals / constraints:
- Simple mental model for product managers and buyers: tiers like Starter / Momentum / Stickiness rather than raw GPU hours.
- Avoid long-term legal complexity: commitments up to 3 months max for standard product.
- Smooth upgrade path to Dedicated (reserved) for high usage customers.
- Preserve incentives for caching/batching (i.e., customers with predictable seq lengths should get better unit economics).

Pricing primitives and definitions (working):
- Token unit: 1 "t" = 1k effective tokens (for simpler numbers); we convert later back to tokens.
- Session credit: 1 session credit = amortization unit for a conversational session (used to model UI-centric customers). Approx 1 session = 8k tokens (8 t) for average chat.
- Commit band: short-term (30d), medium (60d), long (90d) — each has an upfront commitment % and discount ladder.
- Upfront signal options: small payment, trial credits (no discount), or signed PO for larger deals.

Hypothesis: customers prefer a gradual commitment that reduces per-token price by ~15–40% versus PAYG depending on band and upfront.

Baseline PAYG assumptions (internal current numbers, ballpark):
- PAYG price: $0.00004 per token (i.e., $0.04 per 1k tokens == 1 t). So baseline for our 1 t unit = $0.04.
- Average session (mobile chatbot): 8 t -> $0.32 per session.
- Estimated infra cost per 1 t (unit econ): $0.006 (inc GPU, infra amortization, orchestration).
- Gross margin on PAYG: ~85% (very rough).

Commit bands and draft discounts (starting point):
- 30d micro-commit (min $100 upfront): commit signal = $100 spend guarantee over 30d. Discount = 15% off PAYG per t.
- 60d medium-commit (min $500 upfront): spend guarantee over 60d. Discount = 25% off PAYG per t.
- 90d sticky-commit (min $1500 upfront): Discount = 35% off PAYG per t + 5% bonus credits if usage > 80% of commitment.

Mechanics / small-print (how credits interact):
- Credits are consumed in this order: per-request session-cost -> per-token cost -> leftover credits used for additional tokens. (Need to formalize conversion).
- Refunds: none. Unused credits expire at band end. Rollover only by explicit pro-rate swap to a higher band.
- Overages billed PAYG at standard rate (no back-billing).
- Downgrade allowed at band boundary only (so 60d -> 30d at end of cycle).

Conversion heuristics (session <-> token):
- Default conversion: 1 session credit = 8 t (configurable per customer). Onboarding telemetry used to calibrate per-customer average session length.
- When customer selects session-first plan UX, we expose a slider: sessions per month vs expected tokens. Converts to a recommended commit band.

Unit economics quick back-of-envelope (90d band):
- Customer commits $1,500 for 90 days. Discount 35% -> effective price per t = $0.026 (from $0.04).
- If they consume all credits: total effective consumption = $1,500 / $0.026 ≈ 57692 t = 57.7M tokens (since 1 t = 1k tokens -> 57.7B tokens? Wait — careful: 57,692 t * 1k tokens = 57.7M tokens. Correct).
- Infra cost at $0.006 per t => cost = 57,692 * 0.006 ≈ $346.
- Gross margin = ($1,500 - $346) / $1,500 ≈ 77%.
- Compared to PAYG revenue for same usage: PAYG revenue = 57,692 * $0.04 = $2,307 -> so customer saves $807 by committing. We capture less revenue but get upfront cash and higher retention.

Sensitivity checks (if avg session is longer):
- If actual session = 12 t instead of 8 t, customer consumes credits faster; they either top up (pay as they go) or run out and get billed PAYG. Need to ensure we notify at 70% usage and provide pro-rate top-up UX.

Retention / LTV considerations:
- Upfront cash and credit expiry shortens payback window for CAC. If average commit converts to 1.6x retention vs PAYG, that may justify the discount. Need to model LTV/CAC with conversion multipliers.

Operational concerns / product hooks:
- Console UX: clear meter showing committed vs consumed, sessions equivalent, predicted runout date, and one-click top-up.
- Auto-topup toggle (opt-in) to convert to PAYG or to purchase next band at pre-approved discount. Should be off by default.
- Billing: simple invoice showing "commitment credit" line + consumption line.
- SRE: needs to handle burst behavior since customers often cluster tokens early in cycle; consider rate-limited bursts or fair-share. Add soft burst allowances.

Experimentation plan (MVP 60d):
- Offer 60d band with $500 min to a cohort of 200 orgs during onboarding flow. A/B: default PAYG vs suggest commit band. Track conversion, overage rate, churn at 90/120/180 days.
- KPIs: commit conversion %, average consumption as % of commit, overage revenue as % of total, churn delta vs PAYG.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should session-first plans be priced differently for RLHF-heavy use-cases (long seqs) vs short-utterance bots? Probably yes — need per-customer calibration.
- Minimum viable legal terms: do we allow auto-renew? If so, opt-in only, else churn risk at band end.
- How to present the unit math so non-technical buyers understand (Sessions = simpler for product teams). Create a product one-pager.
- Edge-case: customers who are very bursty do they get unfair discount (consume most of commit in week 1)? Consider smoothing credits or weighted decay that unlocks discounts gradually.

Notes on communication / sales play:
- For SMB self-serve, the UX suggestion modal during onboarding: "Save up to 25% with a 60-day commitment" + small calculator.
- For sales-assisted deals, accept signed PO to upgrade to 90d sticky + negotiate custom quantization/latency profiles (bundle services).

Quick UX sketch (copy for modal):
- Title: "Lower cost with a short commitment"
- Body: "Commit to X/month in exchange for Y% off PAYG. Credits are spent first and expire at the end of the period. Don't worry — if you run out, you'll be billed PAYG."
- CTA: "Try 60 days for $500" and a link to "Estimate my usage" (opens a session slider).

Final thoughts: this feels like a low-friction bridge between PAYG and Dedicated. The main value is upfront cash, higher retention signal, and a clear upgrade funnel. Need to validate that our infra risk (bursting) and billing complexity are small compared to revenue uplift.

Action items:
- @Maya run quick modeling: take 50 real trial orgs, estimate 60d commit yield and simulate overage patterns. (Due: 2025-02-14)
- @Hannah prototype modal copy + slider and basic console meter (Due: 2025-02-18)
- Product: confirm billing ledger semantics with finance (no rollover, expire = yes). (Finance owner: TBD)

Rough brain dump ends. Will flesh into a short one-pager + Jira ticket next.
